overview: Venezuela is a country on the northern coast of South America. Its capital and largest city is Caracas. Venezuela won independence from Spain in the early 1800s; Simón Bolívar, who led independence movements across South America, was born in Caracas. Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world.

geography.text: Venezuela has a long Caribbean coastline, with the Andes in the west and the Llanos, wide grassy plains, in the centre. The Orinoco river flows across the country to the Atlantic. In the south-east, flat-topped mountains called tepuis rise from the rainforest, and from one of them falls Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world.

history.text: Venezuela was the birthplace of Simón Bolívar, who led the wars that freed much of South America from Spain. It became fully independent in 1830, after leaving Gran Colombia. Oil, found in the early 1900s, made it rich, but in the 2010s an economic collapse led millions of Venezuelans to leave the country.

events.title: Columbus reaches the coast
events.text: Columbus sails along the coast on his third voyage.

events.title: Oil boom
events.text: A huge oil gusher near Lake Maracaibo begins an oil boom.

events.title: Economic crisis
events.text: A deep crisis begins; millions emigrate over the following years.

government.text: Venezuela is officially a federal presidential republic, but power is concentrated in the government of President Nicolás Maduro, who succeeded Hugo Chávez in 2013. Many countries and international observers did not accept the official results of the 2024 election, which the opposition says it won. Millions of Venezuelans have left the country.

economy.text: Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world, and oil once made it one of the richest countries in Latin America. From 2014 the economy collapsed, with hyperinflation and shortages of food and medicine. US sanctions have limited its oil exports.

culture.text: Venezuela is the birthplace of Simón Bolívar, the liberator of much of South America. Its music includes joropo, played on harp and small guitar. El Sistema, a free music education programme started in 1975, has trained hundreds of thousands of young musicians.

items.title: Angel Falls
items.text: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, 979 metres tall.

items.title: El Sistema
items.text: Youth orchestras that inspired programmes worldwide.

items.title: Arepas
items.text: Corn cakes eaten at almost every meal.

sport.text: Unlike most of South America, Venezuela's favourite sport is baseball, and many Venezuelans have starred in Major League Baseball. Triple jumper Yulimar Rojas has broken the world record and won Olympic gold in 2021.

items.title: Yulimar Rojas
items.text: Triple jump world record holder and Olympic champion.
